title: kithd: blob_download_handler — lazy peer fetch on local miss
description:
Extend blob_download_handler in crates/kithd/src/lib.rs to attempt a peer fetch when the blob is not found locally.

What: wire fetch_peer_blob into the download handler's 404 path.

Algorithm (extends existing handler):
1. Validate blob_id with BlobStore::validate_blob_id(); 400 if invalid (already done)
2. Try to open blob locally (existing code path); if found → serve immediately (no change)
3. If NOT found:
   a. Lock store, call store.get_peer_mailbox_for_blob(blob_id); release lock
   b. If None → 404 (blob is local and missing, or owner-uploaded but gone)
   c. If Some(PeerBlobInfo { mailbox_host, filename, content_type, sha256, size_bytes }):
      - Call fetch_peer_blob(&state.blob_store, &mailbox_host, blob_id, &filename, &content_type, &sha256, size_bytes)
      - If Ok(()):
        * Open the now-cached local blob
        * Serve with correct Content-Type and Content-Disposition
      - If Err(FetchBlobError::Timeout | Network) → 502 Bad Gateway
      - If Err(FetchBlobError::HttpError(404)) → 404 (peer doesn't have it either)
      - If Err(FetchBlobError::HashMismatch | SizeExceeded) → 500 (peer sent corrupt data; log at error level)
      - If Err(FetchBlobError::HostRejected) → 403 (peer host rejected by policy)
      - If Err(FetchBlobError::BlobStore) → 500

Defensive programming:
- Never log the actual blob bytes
- Release store lock before making the network call (do not hold lock across await)
- Use content_type from DB (trusted) not from the peer's HTTP response (untrusted)
- Set Content-Disposition to 'attachment; filename=...' using filename from DB
- Sanitize filename for Content-Disposition header (no control chars, no backslash)

Tests: (integration tests in kithd/tests/, using existing harness)
- Oracle: hardcoded test bytes + sha256 computed with 'echo -n testdata | sha256sum'
- peer attachment served: deliver message with attachment to test kithd; serve mock peer blob; download succeeds
- hash mismatch returns 500: mock peer returns wrong bytes; download returns 500
- unreachable peer returns 502: no server listening at peer host; download returns 502
